chunks: My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said:

Whoever spreads a report against a believer intending thereby to disgrace him and destroy his reputation so that he falls in the eyes of the people — God, Mighty and Majestic, will remove him from His wilaya to the wilaya of Satan.

key_terms.رِوَايَة: a report, narration — here used for spreading damaging information
key_terms.شَيْن: disgrace, harm to reputation; moral blemish
key_terms.مُرُوءَة: muru'ah — the quality of noble, manly virtue; social honour and dignity
key_terms.وَلَايَة: wilaya — guardianship, protective authority; divine patronage vs. Satanic control

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about spreading harmful reports about a believer?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (as) issues a severe warning against spreading harmful reports about believers — whether true or false — when done with the intent to damage their reputation in the eyes of the community. The consequence is spiritually catastrophic: such a person is removed from God's guardianship and placed under the guardianship of Satan. This hadith reflects the Shia emphasis on protecting the honour (muru'ah) of the faithful community and underscores that attacking a believer's social standing is a grave sin with eschatological consequences.

en.bilal-muhammad: My father (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Abi'l Qasim narrated to us from Muhammad b. `Ali al-Kufi from Muhammad b. Sinan from al-Mufaddal b. `Umar from Abi `Abdillah al-Sadiq (as). He said:

Whoever reports something about a believer intending for him to be harmed and for his reputation to be destroyed so that he may fall in the eyes of the people, Allah will take him out of His wilaya and put him in the wilaya of Satan.
